## Purpose

This procedure describes the safe operation, temperature programming,
and maintenance of the muffle furnace used in the EA Program
laboratory. The muffle furnace provides controlled high-temperature
combustion (up to 1,100 C) for loss-on-ignition analysis
([SOP-L406](SOP-L406-loss-on-ignition.qmd)), pre-combustion of
crucibles and glass fiber filters, ashing of organic materials, and
flux fusion preparations.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All use of muffle furnaces in EA Program
  laboratories, including routine ignition (550 C for SOM), high-
  temperature ashing (up to 1,000 C), and pre-combustion of labware
- **Does not apply to:** Drying ovens operating below 300 C (see
  [SOP-L105](SOP-L105-drying-ovens.qmd)); tube furnaces for
  elemental analysis (integral to analytical instruments); kilns
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 134

## Definitions

- **Ashing:** High-temperature combustion of organic matter in an open
  crucible in the muffle furnace, leaving only the inorganic (mineral)
  residue; the basis of loss-on-ignition analysis.
- **Crucible:** A heat-resistant container (ceramic, porcelain, or
  platinum) used to hold samples during furnace ignition; must be
  pre-ignited to constant mass before use.
- **Loss on ignition (LOI):** The mass loss when a dried sample is
  ignited at 550 °C for 4 hours, expressed as a percentage of dry mass;
  used as a proxy for soil organic matter content.
- **Muffle:** The interior chamber of the furnace, thermally isolated
  from the heating elements; provides a controlled oxidizing atmosphere
  for combustion.
- **Pre-combustion:** Heating glassware, crucibles, or glass fiber
  filters to 450--550 °C to destroy any organic contamination before
  use in carbon or organic matter analyses.
- **Ramping:** Programming the furnace to increase temperature at a
  controlled rate (e.g., 5 °C min^-1^) to prevent thermal shock to
  crucibles and to avoid rapid oxidation that can cause sample loss.
- **Set point temperature:** The target temperature programmed into the
  furnace controller; verify with a calibrated thermocouple if precise
  temperature is critical.

## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, authorize furnace use          |
| Lab Manager       | Schedule maintenance, verify thermocouple calibration |
| Trained Personnel | Operate the furnace per this SOP            |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Thermal:** The furnace exterior, door, and chamber reach extremely
  high temperatures. Crucibles removed from the furnace at 550 C or
  above can cause severe burns on contact. The furnace remains hot for
  hours after shutdown.
- **Fire:** Combustible materials (paper, wood, plastic) placed on or
  near the furnace can ignite. Keep a 30 cm clear zone around the
  furnace on all sides.
- **Fumes:** Combustion of organic matter produces CO~2~, water vapor,
  and potentially odorous or irritating fumes. Ensure adequate room
  ventilation or connect the furnace exhaust to a fume hood or duct
  if available.
- **Electrical:** The furnace draws high current. Do not use extension
  cords. Inspect the power cord for damage before each use.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Heat-resistant gloves (rated to at least 500 C)
- [ ] Safety glasses or face shield
- [ ] Lab coat (cotton preferred; synthetic fabrics melt)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes

### Emergency Procedures

For burns, apply cool running water immediately and seek first aid.
If the furnace produces unusual smoke, odors, or sparks, shut it off
at the circuit breaker and evacuate the room. Refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd).


## Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Muffle furnace (programmable)         | SGM 134; confirm maximum temperature rating |
| Crucible tongs (long-handled, heat-rated) | For placing and retrieving crucibles |
| Ceramic crucibles or porcelain boats  | Pre-combusted before first use |
| Heat-resistant pad or ceramic tile    | For resting hot crucibles during transfer to desiccator |
| Desiccator with active desiccant      | For cooling crucibles before weighing |
| Thermocouple or secondary thermometer | For periodic temperature verification |


## Procedure

### Pre-Use Inspection

1. Inspect the furnace chamber for debris, cracked insulation, or
   damage to the heating elements. Do not operate if damage is visible;
   report to the lab manager.
2. Verify that the area around the furnace is clear of combustible
   materials (minimum 30 cm clearance on all sides and top)
3. Confirm that the furnace is plugged directly into a dedicated wall
   outlet (no extension cords or power strips)

### Loading

1. Arrange crucibles or boats inside the chamber so they do not touch
   each other or the heating elements. Leave space for air circulation.
2. Close the furnace door gently; do not slam (the refractory lining
   is fragile)

### Temperature Programming

1. Set the target temperature and ramp rate per the analytical SOP:
   - Loss on ignition (SOP-L406): ramp to 550 C, hold 4 hours
   - Pre-combustion of glass fiber filters: ramp to 450 C, hold
     4 hours
   - Pre-combustion of crucibles: ramp to 550 C, hold 1 hour
   - Ceramic boat preparation (SSM, SOP-L407): ramp to 900 C, hold
     30 minutes
2. If the furnace is programmable, set the ramp rate to approximately
   10 C per minute unless the analytical SOP specifies otherwise
3. Start the program and verify that the displayed temperature begins
   to rise

::: {.callout-tip}
Avoid placing samples into a furnace that is already at full
temperature unless the analytical SOP explicitly requires it. Rapid
thermal shock can crack crucibles and cause spattering.
:::

### During Operation

1. Do not leave the furnace unattended during the initial ramp-up
   (first 30 minutes). Check that the temperature is tracking the
   set point.
2. Post a "Furnace in Use" sign on the furnace and the lab door,
   noting the expected completion time
3. Do not open the furnace door during the hold period unless
   troubleshooting

### Unloading

1. After the hold period, turn off the furnace or allow the programmed
   cooldown to proceed
2. Allow the furnace to cool to below 200 C before opening the door.
   Opening at higher temperatures causes rapid thermal shock to
   samples and exposes the operator to radiant heat.
3. Using crucible tongs and heat-resistant gloves, transfer crucibles
   to a heat-resistant pad, then immediately to the desiccator
4. Allow crucibles to cool to room temperature in the desiccator
   (approximately 30--45 minutes) before weighing

### Shutdown

1. Verify that the furnace is off and the temperature is decreasing
2. Remove the "Furnace in Use" sign
3. Leave the furnace door slightly ajar (1--2 cm) after it has cooled
   below 100 C to prevent moisture buildup inside the chamber


## Maintenance

| Task                                  | Frequency              |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------|
| Visual inspection of chamber and elements | Before each use    |
| Clean furnace floor of spilled material | After each use       |
| Thermocouple verification (compare to NIST-traceable thermometer) | Annually or after suspected malfunction |
| Replace heating elements              | As needed (contact manufacturer or lab manager) |
| Check door seal and gasket            | Every 6 months         |

::: {.callout-important}
Never use water or wet cloths to clean the furnace interior. Allow the
chamber to cool completely, then brush out ash and debris with a dry,
soft brush.
:::


## Quality Control

- Verify furnace temperature with an independent thermocouple or
  NIST-traceable thermometer at least annually. The furnace set point
  and the verified temperature should agree within +/- 10 C at 550 C.
- Record the verification date and result in the instrument logbook.
- If temperature uniformity is critical (e.g., for large batches),
  place thermocouples at the front, center, and back of the chamber
  and record any gradient.


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Combusted soil ash            | Standard trash (inert mineral residue)   |
| Crucibles                     | Clean and reuse                          |
| Failed heating elements       | E-waste; coordinate with campus facilities |

## Training Record

Before operating the muffle furnace independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Demonstrate proper use of heat-resistant gloves and crucible tongs
4. Load, program, and unload the furnace under supervision for one
   complete cycle
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
